A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RegCache study. All 28 pages of v4 and 32 pages of v5, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, support comparison. Renumbered and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v4 reports original classification, retrieval, image/video VLM, segmentation, latency and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results and adds comparisons with simpler heuristics and additional hyperparameter-sensitivity results.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same sensitive-layer selection, register curation, averaged KV-cache prefixing and token deletion procedure. Equations (1)–(2) and the existing reconstruction-loss and FP16 variants are unchanged. Added controls and search documentation do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: The classification, retrieval, image/video understanding, segmentation and LLM diagnostic coverage is retained. The new heuristic comparisons and parameter sweeps reuse ImageNet-1k; they introduce no new dataset, task or input environment.

E2.justification: v5 Appendix H/Table 13 adds random sink-token prefixing and outlier clipping as evaluated comparators on CLIP-B/16 under W8A8 quantization. The existing PTQ baselines, test-time registers and other appendix comparators remain.

E3.justification: v5 adds one-parameter-at-a-time sensitivity experiments reported for SigLIP2, including sweeps through 30 prefix tokens and 20 deleted tokens, plus defined heuristic-control procedures in Appendix H. Existing benchmark splits, calibration sample counts and quantization settings are retained. Appendix E's default search ranges are additional documentation.

E4.justification: v4 Appendix J's insertion-layer analysis expands into v5 Appendix K's five-panel study, adding sensitivity to prefix count, deletion count, critical-layer selection and candidate-pool size. New Appendix H also tests whether curated registers outperform random prefixing and direct clipping. Together these substantially broaden the analysis of tuning sensitivity and design choices.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same 64-image cosine-similarity analysis and ± summaries. The added comparisons and sensitivity plots introduce no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: New Table 13 reports 54.18% for random prefixing and 47.29% for clipping, alongside the retained 59.71% RegCache result. Figure 8 adds parameter-dependent results. The reconstruction-loss table changes the NoisyQuant CLIP-B/16 W8A8 baseline from 63.62 to 63.20 (v4 Table 14; v5 Table 16). Main benchmark and latency values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The method equations and Appendix F's Lemma 1, assumptions and proof, including Equations (3)–(6), are unchanged. The expanded explanatory discussion introduces no new formal derivation.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces a universal register usable for any input with reusable registers for other inputs, modestly narrowing the generality claim. The central claims of training-free, complementary PTQ improvement through middle-layer prefixing and deletion remain.

C2.justification: v5 adds explanations for smaller gains with high bitwidths and strong PTQ baselines, and a softmax-related interpretation of differences between models. Appendices H and K interpret the new controls and sweeps through register generality, excessive-prefix noise and deletion-related information loss. The existing hyperparameter-tuning limitations remain.

D1.justification: New Appendices E.3–E.4 summarize the four-layer extraction search, maximum 15 prefix tokens and maximum 10 deleted tokens, describe sequential sweeps, and clarify preprocessing per model, PTQ baseline and bitwidth. The deletion limit is newly disclosed; the other ranges were already stated or implied. Hardware and calibration details are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds an explicit comparison with Son et al.'s KV-cache prefixing, distinguishing data-driven candidates, middle-layer caching and deletion, and sharpens the comparison with test-time registers. References to Improved Baselines with Visual Instruction Tuning and LLaVA-NeXT are removed, although their model evaluations remain.

P1.justification: v5 makes targeted prose edits, changes universality terminology to reusability/generalizability, reorganizes related-work paragraphs, and adds an appendix contents page and numbered experimental-detail subsections. Affiliation and funding text also change. The overall narrative structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn and relabeled. Figure 8 becomes a five-panel display incorporating the earlier insertion-layer curve and highlighting selected settings. Two tables are added, the classification and VLM tables exchange numbers 4 and 5, and existing displays are repositioned. Most figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The added controls and sensitivity analyses strengthen support for design choices, while explicit search details and more qualified transfer claims improve reproducibility and clarity. These benefits outweigh a localized numerical inconsistency: after the baseline correction in Table 16, the CLIP-B/16 W8A8 best/average gaps remain +2.18/+0.61, although its rows imply +2.60/about +0.70. The main empirical conclusions remain unchanged.
